input: In EnergyPlus, what does the UpdateSysSizing(EndSysSizingCalc) function calculate?
output: The UpdateSysSizing(EndSysSizingCalc) function calculates for each system the peak heating and cooling loads and flow rates over all the sizing periods.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what concludes the tasks of the Sizing Manager?
output: The end of the tasks of the Sizing Manager is indicated after all sizing calculations are completed.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the focus of the section labeled 'System Design Loads and Air Flow Rates'?
output: The section focuses on System Design Loads and Air Flow Rates.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the system design calculation?
output: The purpose of the system design calculation is to estimate design heating and cooling loads and air flow rates for each air loop in the simulation problem.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the calculation sequence for system level design loads and air flow rates compare to that for zone loads and air flow rates?
output: The calculation sequence for system level design loads and air flow rates resembles the calculation sequence for zone loads and air flow rates.

input: In EnergyPlus, when is the update subroutine UpdateSysSizing called during the sizing process?
output: The update subroutine UpdateSysSizing is called at the beginning, during, and end of a loop in the Sizing Manager over all the design days.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the major difference between system design calculation and zone calculation?
output: The major difference is that the system design calculation is done at the zone time-step only, while the zone calculation triggers an idealized component calculation at the system time-step.

input: In EnergyPlus, what data does the system design calculation operate with?
output: The system design calculation operates at the zone time step using the design environment weather data and the data stored in the zone sizing arrays.

input: According to EnergyPlus, where are the results of the system design calculation stored?
output: The results of the system design calculation are stored in the system sizing arrays.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does SysSizInput(i) store?
output: SysSizInput(i) stores the input data from the Sizing:System objects.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does SysSizing(i,j) represent?
output: SysSizing(i,j) stores the results of the system design calculations for all systems and all design days.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does CalcSysSizing(i) store?
output: CalcSysSizing(i) stores the results of the system design calculations for the peak heating and cooling cases for each air loop.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does FinalSysSizing(i) differ from CalcSysSizing(i)?
output: FinalSysSizing(i) corresponds to CalcSysSizing but includes the effect of the user specified sizing factor or user specified system design flow rate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what type of data does SysSizing include?
output: The data stored in SysSizing includes the coincident peak cooling mass flow rate, coincident peak heating mass flow rate, noncoincident peak cooling mass flow rate, noncoincident peak heating mass flow rate, design main supply duct volume flow, design heat supply duct volume flow, design cool supply duct volume flow, design sensible cooling capacity, design total cooling capacity, design heating capacity, design preheat capacity, mixed air temperature at the time of the cooling peak, mixed air humidity ratio at the time of the cooling peak, return air temperature at the time of the cooling peak, return air humidity ratio at the time of the cooling peak, outside air temperature at the time of the cooling peak, outside air humidity ratio at the time of the cooling peak, design mixed air temperature for heating, design mixed air humidity ratio for heating, design return air temperature for heating, design return air humidity ratio for heating, design outside air temperature for heating, design outside air humidity ratio for heating, daily sequence of system heating air mass flow rate, daily sequence of system cooling air mass flow rate, daily sequence of zones' summed cooling load, daily sequence of zones flow weighted average temperature, daily sequence of system sensible cooling capacity, daily sequence of system total cooling capacity, daily sequence of system heating capacity, daily sequence of system preheat capacity, and daily sequence of system cooling return temperatures.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does CoinCoolMassFlow represent?
output: CoinCoolMassFlow represents the coincident peak cooling mass flow rate in kg/s.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the unit for DesMainVolFlow?
output: DesMainVolFlow is measured in cubic meters per second (m³/s).

input: From EnergyPlus, what does SensCoolCap indicate?
output: SensCoolCap indicates the design sensible cooling capacity in watts (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does MixTempAtCoolPeak represent?
output: MixTempAtCoolPeak represents the mixed air temperature at the time of the cooling peak in degrees Celsius (C).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does HeatMixTemp refer to?
output: HeatMixTemp refers to the design mixed air temperature for heating in degrees Celsius (C).

input: From EnergyPlus, what does HeatFlowSeq(i) store?
output: HeatFlowSeq(i) stores the daily sequence of system heating air mass flow rate in kg/s.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does CoolZoneAvgTempSeq(I) represent?
output: CoolZoneAvgTempSeq(I) represents the daily sequence of zones' flow weighted average temperature in watts (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does SysCoolRetHumRatSeq(I) represent?
output: SysCoolRetHumRatSeq(I) represents the daily sequence of system cooling return humidity ratios (zone time step) measured in kg water/kg dry air.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is represented by SysHeatRetTempSeq(i)?
output: SysHeatRetTempSeq(i) represents the daily sequence of system heating return temperatures (zone time step) measured in degrees Celsius.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does SysHeatRetHumRatSeq(I) indicate?
output: SysHeatRetHumRatSeq(I) indicates the daily sequence of system heating return humidity ratios (zone time step) measured in kg water/kg dry air.

input: In EnergyPlus, what information does SysCoolOutTempSeq provide?
output: SysCoolOutTempSeq provides the daily sequence of system cooling outside temperatures (zone time step) measured in degrees Celsius.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does SysCoolOutHumRatSeq represent?
output: SysCoolOutHumRatSeq represents the daily sequence of system cooling outside humidity ratios (zone time step) measured in kg water/kg dry air.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does SysHeatOutTempSeq indicate?
output: SysHeatOutTempSeq indicates the daily sequence of system heating outside temperatures (zone time step) measured in degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is represented by SysHeatOutHumRatSeq?
output: SysHeatOutHumRatSeq represents the daily sequence of system heating outside humidity ratios (zone time step) measured in kg water/kg dry air.

input: In EnergyPlus, how are system design loads and flow rates calculated?
output: System design loads and flow rates are calculated using the zone level results.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if latent sizing is requested and latent loads are greater than sensible loads?
output: The latent design load and air mass flow rate are used for that zone.

input: In EnergyPlus, how are the zone design flow rates for zones served by an air loop obtained?
output: The zone design flow rates for the zones served by an air loop are summed to obtain the system level design flow rates.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is mixed with the system level design minimum outside air flow rate?
output: The summed zone design flow rates are mixed with the system level design minimum outside air flow rate to obtain system design coil loads.

input: In EnergyPlus, which subroutine performs the activities related to system sizing calculations?
output: The activities are performed within the UpdateSysSizing subroutine in the SimAirServingZones module.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when is the UpdateSysSizing subroutine called?
output: It is called at the start of each design day, at the zone time-step, at the end of the design day, and at the end of the zone design calculation.

input: In EnergyPlus, what logical flag corresponds to ZoneSizingCalc?
output: The logical flag SysSizingCalc corresponds to ZoneSizingCalc.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does any reference to a 'zone' equate to in this context?
output: Any reference to a 'zone' is equivalent to 'air terminal unit'.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is stored in the system sizing data structures at the beginning of a design day?
output: The environment name is stored in the system sizing data structures.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is NonCoinCoolMassFlow_sys calculated?
output: NonCoinCoolMassFlow_sys is calculated as the sum of DesCoolMassFlow_zone.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is NonCoinHeatMassFlow_sys calculated?
output: NonCoinHeatMassFlow_sys is calculated as the sum of DesHeatMassFlow_zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is CoolFlowSeq_sys(i) determined?
output: CoolFlowSeq_sys(i) is determined as the sum of CoolFlowSeq_zone(i).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is SysCoolRetTemp(i) calculated?
output: SysCoolRetTemp(i) is calculated as the sum of CoolZoneRetTempSeq(i) multiplied by CoolFlowSeq_zone(i), divided by CoolFlowSeq_sys(i).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is SysCoolRetHumRat(i) determined?
output: SysCoolRetHumRat(i) is determined as the sum of CoolZoneHumRatSeq(i) multiplied by CoolFlowSeq_zone(i), divided by CoolFlowSeq_sys(i).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is FracOA calculated?
output: FracOA is calculated as the product of the density of air and DesOutAirVolFlow_sys divided by CoolFlowSeq_sys(i).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is T_mix?
output: T_mix is calculated as T_outside multiplied by FracOA plus SysCoolRetTemp(i) multiplied by (1 - FracOA).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is W_mix calculated?
output: W_mix is calculated as W_outside multiplied by FracOA plus SysCoolRetHumRat(i) multiplied by (1 - FracOA).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does SysCoolOutTempSeq(i) represent?
output: SysCoolOutTempSeq(i) represents T_outside.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is SysCoolOutHumRatSeq(i) defined?
output: SysCoolOutHumRatSeq(i) is defined as W_outside.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is SysSensCoolCap_cur calculated?
output: SysSensCoolCap_cur is calculated as C_p,air multiplied by CoolFlowSeq_sys(i) multiplied by (T_mix - T_sup).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is SensCoolCapSeq(I)?
output: SensCoolCapSeq(I) is defined as SysSensCoolCap_cur.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when is SysSensCoolCap_cur saved as the design value?
output: SysSensCoolCap_cur is saved as the design value if it is the maximum for the day so far.

input: In EnergyPlus, what do CoolMixTemp_sys, CoolMixHumRat_sys, CoolRetTemp_sys, CoolRetHumRat_sys, CoolOutTemp_sys, and CoolOutHumRat_sys represent?
output: They represent the corresponding mixed, return, and outside conditions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does ρ_air represent?
output: ρ_air is the density of dry air at 20°C and standard elevation corrected pressure.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is FracOA?
output: FracOA is the outside air fraction.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does C_p,air signify?
output: C_p,air signifies the specific heat of dry air at 20°C.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does T\\(_{sup}\\) represent?
output: T\\(_{sup}\\) is the user specified design cooling supply temperature {[}C{]}.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does T\\(_{mix}\\) refer to?
output: T\\(_{mix}\\) is the current mixed air temperature {[}C{]}.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is W\\(_{mix}\\)?
output: W\\(_{mix}\\) is the current mixed air humidity ratio {[}kg water / kg dry air{]}.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is T\\(_{outside}\\)?
output: T\\(_{outside}\\) is the current outside air temperature {[}C{]}.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does W\\(_{outside}\\) represent?
output: W\\(_{outside}\\) is the current outside air humidity ratio {[}kg water / kg dry air{]}.

input: In EnergyPlus, when is the system cooling coil outlet air humidity ratio used as w\\(_{sup}\\)?
output: The system cooling coil outlet air humidity ratio is used as w\\(_{sup}\\) when latent sizing is requested.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the system cooling coil outlet air humidity ratio calculated?
output: The system cooling coil outlet air humidity ratio is calculated as a mass flow rate weighted average of each zone's latent cooling supply air humidity ratio.

input: In EnergyPlus, when is the calculated value for the system cooling coil outlet air humidity ratio used?
output: This calculated value is used only when one or more zone latent load is found to be greater than that zone's sensible load, or latent only sizing is requested.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is suggested to enable the system cooling coil to dehumidify?
output: A control method that enables the system cooling coil to dehumidify to the design latent supply air humidity ratio is suggested.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does SysHeatRetTemp(i) represent?
output: SysHeatRetTemp(i) is the sum of HeatZoneRetTempSeq(i) multiplied by HeatFlowSeq\\(_{zone}\\)(i) divided by HeatFlowSeq\\(_{sys}\\)(i).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the current system heating capacity calculated?
output: SysHeatCap\\(_{cur}\\) is calculated as C\\(_{p,air}\\) * MinFlowRat\\(_{sys}\\) * HeatFlowSeq\\(_{sys}\\)(i) * (T\\(_{sup}\\) - T\\(_{mix}\\)).

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens if SysHeatCap\\(_{cur}\\) is the maximum for the day?
output: If SysHeatCap\\(_{cur}\\) is the maximum for the day so far, then SysHeatCap\\(_{cur}\\) is saved as the design value.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does DesCoolVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\) represent when coincident system sizing is specified?
output: DesCoolVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\) is calculated as \\(\\rho\\(_{air}\\) * CoinCoolMassFlow\\(_{sys}\\).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is DesMainVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\) determined when noncoincident system sizing is specified?
output: DesMainVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\) is determined as Max(DesCoolVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\), DesHeatVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\)).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is modified based on the outdoor air method selected?
output: The DesCoolVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\) and DesHeatVolFlow\\(_{sys}\\) are modified based on the system ventilation efficiency calculated based on the maximum outdoor air fraction.

input: In EnergyPlus, what calculations have been completed at the point of EndSysSizingCalc?
output: All the calculations have been done in SysSizing(i,j) and results for each design day have been obtained.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the first step for coincident sizing in EndSysSizingCalc?
output: The first step is to loop over all of the air loops.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done if DesCoolVolFlow in SysSizing for the current design day is greater than the value stored in CalcSysSizing?
output: Move DesCoolVolFlow from SysSizing into CalcSysSizing along with several specified parameters.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what parameters should be moved into CalcSysSizing along with DesCoolVolFlow?
output: The parameters include CoolDesDay, CoinCoolMassFlow, SensCoolCap, CoolFlowSeq(i), SensCoolCapSeq(i), CoolMixTemp, CoolRetTemp, CoolMixHumRat, CoolRetHumRat, CoolOutTemp, CoolOutHumRat, SysCoolRetTempSeq(i), SysCoolRetHumRatSeq(i), SysCoolOutTempSeq(i), and SysCoolOutHumRatSeq(i).

input: In EnergyPlus, what action should be taken if DesHeatVolFlow in SysSizing for the current design day is greater than the value stored in CalcSysSizing?
output: Move DesHeatVolFlow from SysSizing into CalcSysSizing along with several specified parameters.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what parameters should be moved into CalcSysSizing along with DesHeatVolFlow?
output: The parameters include HeatDesDay, CoinHeatMassFlow, HeatCap, PreHeatCap, HeatFlowSeq(i), HeatCapSeq(i), PreHeatCapSeq(i), HeatMixTemp, HeatRetTemp, HeatMixHumRat, HeatRetHumRat, HeatOutTemp, HeatOutHumRat, SysHeatRetTempSeq(i), SysHeatRetHumRatSeq(i), SysHeatOutTempSeq(i), and SysHeatOutHumRatSeq(i).

input: In EnergyPlus, where is the peak cooling and peak heating data stored after processing all design days?
output: The peak cooling and peak heating data will be stored in CalcSysSizing.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is DesMainVolFlow in CalcSysSizing determined?
output: DesMainVolFlow in CalcSysSizing is set equal to the maximum of DesCoolVolFlow and DesHeatVolFlow.

input: In EnergyPlus, what makes the task harder for noncoincident sizing?
output: The task is harder because there isn't a single time-step during which all the zone peaks occur.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what must be calculated for noncoincident sizing due to the absence of obvious peak values?
output: Average values for return and outside conditions must be calculated.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the next step after looping over all the zones cooled by the air loop?
output: In FinalZoneSizing, replace the value in DesCoolCoilInTemp with the user-specified CoolSupTemp(sys).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should be done for DesCoolCoilInHumRat and CoolSupHumRat in FinalZoneSizing?
output: Replace the value in DesCoolCoilInHumRat with the user specified CoolSupHumRat.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is NonCoinCoolMassFlow(sys) calculated?
output: NonCoinCoolMassFlow(sys) is calculated as the sum of DesCoolMassFlow(zone).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is SysCoolRetTemp calculated?
output: SysCoolRetTemp is calculated as (ZoneRetTempAtCoolPeak * DesCoolMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinCoolMassFlow(sys).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is SysCoolRetHumRat determined?
output: SysCoolRetHumRat is determined as (ZoneHumRatAtCoolPeak * DesCoolMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinCoolMassFlow(sys).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the formula for calculating SysCoolOutTemp?
output: SysCoolOutTemp is calculated as (T(OA,zone peak) * DesCoolMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinCoolMassFlow(sys).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is SysCoolOutHumRat calculated?
output: SysCoolOutHumRat is calculated as (W(OA,zone peak) * DesCoolMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinCoolMassFlow(sys).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is calculated at the end of the zone loop?
output: Mixed air conditions and the system sensible cooling capacity are calculated.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is FracOA calculated?
output: FracOA is calculated as ρ(air) * DesOutAirVolFlow(sys) / NonCoinCoolMassFlow(sys).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the formula for T(mix)?
output: T(mix) is calculated as SysCoolOutTemp * FracOA + SysCoolRetTemp * (1 - FracOA).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is W(mix) calculated?
output: W(mix) is calculated as SysCoolOutHumRat * FracOA + SysCoolRetHumRat * (1 - FracOA).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is SysSensCoolCap determined?
output: SysSensCoolCap is determined as C(p,air) * NonCoinCoolMassFlow * (T(mix) - T(sup)).

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens to the variables calculated in section (ii) for noncoincident sizing?
output: The variables calculated in section (ii) are moved into the CalcSysSizing Array.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the first step when processing the air loop for zones?
output: Loop over all of the zones heated by this air loop.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should be replaced in FinalZoneSizing with the user specified HeatSupTemp?
output: The value in DesHeatCoilInTemp should be replaced with the user specified HeatSupTemp.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is ensured by replacing DesHeatCoilInTemp, DesHeatCoilInHumRat, and HeatSupHumRat?
output: It ensures that zone equipment connected to an air loop will use the system design supply air conditions as coil entering conditions.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is NonCoinHeatMassFlow defined?
output: NonCoinHeatMassFlow is defined as the sum of DesHeatMassFlow for all zones.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is SysHeatRetTemp calculated?
output: SysHeatRetTemp is calculated as (ZoneRetTempAtHeatPeak * DesHeatMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinHeatMassFlow(sys).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is SysHeatRetHumRat calculated?
output: SysHeatRetHumRat is calculated as (ZoneHumRatAtHeatPeak * DesHeatMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinHeatMassFlow(sys).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the formula for SysHeatOutTemp?
output: SysHeatOutTemp is calculated as (T(OA,zone peak) * DesHeatMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinHeatMassFlow(sys).

input: From EnergyPlus, how is SysHeatOutHumRat calculated?
output: SysHeatOutHumRat is calculated as (W(OA,zone peak) * DesHeatMassFlow(zone)) / NonCoinHeatMassFlow(sys).

input: In EnergyPlus, what must be calculated at the end of the zone loop?
output: Mixed air conditions and the system sensible cooling capacity must be calculated at the end of the zone loop.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is FracOA defined?
output: FracOA is defined as the product of the density of air and DesOutAirVolFlow(sys) divided by NonCoinHeatMassFlow(sys).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is T(mix) calculated?
output: T(mix) is calculated as SysHeatOutTemp * FracOA + SysHeatRetTemp * (1 - FracOA).

input: From EnergyPlus, how is W(mix) calculated?
output: W(mix) is calculated as SysHeatOutHumRat * FracOA + SysHeatRetHumRat * (1 - FracOA).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the formula for SysHeatlCap?
output: SysHeatlCap is calculated as C(p,air) * NonCoinHeatlMassFlow * (T(sup) - T(mix)).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens to the variables calculated in section (ii) for noncoincident sizing?
output: The variables calculated in section (ii) are moved into the CalcSysSizing Array.

input: In EnergyPlus, what must be done with the calculated system sizing data from CalcSysSizing?
output: The calculated system sizing data must be moved into the FinalSysSizing array.

input: From EnergyPlus, how are user specified system design flow rates turned into sizing ratios?
output: User specified system design flow rates are turned into sizing ratios by dividing the user input value by the calculated value.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is CoinCoolMassFlow calculated?
output: CoinCoolMassFlow is calculated as SizRat(cool) multiplied by CoinCoolMassFlow(calc).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is NonCoinCoolMassFlow defined?
output: NonCoinCoolMassFlow is defined as SizRat(cool) multiplied by NonCoinCoolMassFlow(calc).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is DesCoolVolFlow calculated?
output: DesCoolVolFlow is calculated as SizRat(cool) multiplied by DesCoolVolFlow(calc).

input: From EnergyPlus, what must be done for the time-step sequence and for the peak value?
output: The outside air fraction must be recalculated, which will alter the design mixed air conditions and lead to an altered value for the cooling capacity.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is CoolFlowSeq(sys)(i) calculated?
output: CoolFlowSeq(sys)(i) is calculated as SizRat(cool) multiplied by CoolFlowSeq(sys,calc)(i).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is FracOA recalculated during the zone timesteps?
output: FracOA is recalculated as the product of the density of air and DesOutAirVolFlow(sys) divided by CoolFlowSeq(sys)(i).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is T(mix) recalculated during the zone timesteps?
output: T(mix) is recalculated as SysCoolOutTempSeq(i) multiplied by FracOA plus SysCoolRetTempSeq(i) multiplied by (1 - FracOA).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Sensible Cooling Capacity for a sequence defined?
output: The Sensible Cooling Capacity for a sequence is defined as SensCoolCapSeq(i) = C_{p,air} * CoolFlowSeq_{sys}(i) * (T_{mix} - T_{sup}).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should be calculated for peak cooling?
output: For peak cooling, the same calculation as for the sensible cooling capacity should be performed.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the fraction of outdoor air calculated?
output: The fraction of outdoor air (FracOA) is calculated as FracOA = ρ_{air} * DesOutAirVolFlow_{sys} / DesCoolVolFlow.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the mixed temperature calculated?
output: The mixed temperature (T_{mix}) is calculated as T_{mix} = CoolOutTemp_{sys} * FracOA + CoolRetTemp_{sys} * (1 - FracOA).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the mixed humidity ratio determined?
output: The mixed humidity ratio (W_{mix}) is determined as W_{mix} = CoolOutHumRat_{sys} * FracOA + CoolRetHumRat_{sys} * (1 - FracOA).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Sensible Cooling Capacity for the system defined?
output: The Sensible Cooling Capacity for the system is defined as SensCoolCap_{sys} = C_{p,air} * DesCoolVolFlow_{sys} * (T_{mix} - T_{sup}).

input: In EnergyPlus, where are T_{mix} and W_{mix} saved?
output: T_{mix} and W_{mix} are saved in FinalSysSizing.

input: From EnergyPlus, what should be calculated for the heating case?
output: For the heating case, the same calculation as for the cooling case should be performed.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Coincident Heating Mass Flow calculated?
output: The Coincident Heating Mass Flow is calculated as CoinHeatMassFlow = SizRat_{heat} * CoinHeatMassFlow_{calc}.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Non-Coincident Heating Mass Flow calculated?
output: The Non-Coincident Heating Mass Flow is calculated as NonCoinHeatMassFlow = SizRat_{heat} * NonCoinHeatMassFlow_{calc}.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Design Heating Volume Flow calculated?
output: The Design Heating Volume Flow is calculated as DesHeatVolFlow = SizRat_{heat} * DesHeatVolFlow_{calc}.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the formula for HeatFlowSeq_{sys}(i)?
output: HeatFlowSeq_{sys}(i) = SizRat_{Heat} * HeatFlowSeq_{sys,calc}(i).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the fraction of outdoor air for heating calculated?
output: The fraction of outdoor air for heating (FracOA) is calculated as FracOA = ρ_{air} * DesOutAirVolFlow_{sys} / HeatFlowSeq_{sys}(i).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the mixed temperature for heating calculated?
output: The mixed temperature for heating (T_{mix}) is calculated as T_{mix} = SysHeatOutTempSeq(i) * FracOA + SysHeatRetTempSeq(i) * (1 - FracOA).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the heating capacity sequence defined?
output: The heating capacity sequence is defined as HeatCapSeq(i) = C_{p,air} * HeatFlowSeq_{sys}(i) * (T_{sup} - T_{mix}).

input: From EnergyPlus, what should be calculated for peak heating?
output: For peak heating, the same calculation as for the heating capacity sequence should be performed.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Design Main Volume Flow calculated?
output: The Design Main Volume Flow is calculated as DesMainVolFlow_{sys} = MAX(DesCoolVolFlow_{sys}, DesHeatVolFlow_{sys}).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what information is stored regarding the dominant flow for each air loop?
output: The program stores which was dominant for each air loop in the boolean data structure variables sysSizeCoolingDominant and sysSizeHeatingDominant.

input: In EnergyPlus, what adjustments are made to system air flow sizes based on the operation of zone air terminals?
output: Additional adjustments are made to system air flow sizes based on details of how the zone air terminals connected to the system will eventually operate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, in which version were system sizing adjustments for air terminal operation added?
output: System sizing adjustments were added as of version 8.9 of EnergyPlus.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the basic idea behind system sizing adjustments for air terminal operation?
output: The basic idea is to account for operating details of the air terminal units attached to the system by making adjustments to the system sizing results after the zone equipment has been setup and sized.

input: In EnergyPlus, which routine is responsible for managing system sizing adjustments?
output: The routine ManageSystemSizingAdjustments is responsible for managing system sizing adjustments.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the ManageSystemSizingAdjustments routine do first?
output: The ManageSystemSizingAdjustments routine first sets up the zone equipment.

input: From EnergyPlus, what information does the ManageSystemSizingAdjustments routine mine to improve accuracy and robustness?
output: The routine mines information from the air terminal models for minimum flow fractions, operating modes during heating, and any user-defined hard sizes.

input: In EnergyPlus, how do actual operating flow rates during heating compare to the design heating flow rate derived from zone loads?
output: The actual operating flow rates during heating are often quite different from the design heating flow rate derived from the zone loads.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the adjustment method do to develop accurate values for flow rates during heating operation?
output: The adjustment method scans all the air terminals and develops accurate values for the minimum and maximum flow rates that will occur during heating operation.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the system design heating flow rate adjusted?
output: The system design heating flow rate is adjusted to reflect the new results developed from the adjustment method.

input: From EnergyPlus, in a VAV system with Normal action dampers that is cooling dominated, how is the heating design flow rate determined?
output: The heating design flow rate is determined as the cooling design flow rate times the minimum flow fraction at the dampers.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what needs to be adjusted when heating loads dominate in a system?
output: The cooling design flow rate needs to be adjusted to account for how the terminals will really operate during cooling rather than the cooling-load-based sizing result.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the ManageSystemSizingAdjustments routine do for each airloop?
output: The routine loops over all the zones attached to that air loop.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the three summed values for terminal air flows reported to the EIO and table summary report?
output: The three summed values are: (1) minimum flow rate during heating operation, (2) maximum flow rate during heating operation, and (3) maximum flow rate.

input: From EnergyPlus, what determines the type of zone sum to use in the Sizing:System input object?
output: The type of zone sum to use can be either noncoincident or coincident, determined in the input field called Type of Zone Sum to Use.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the design system heating flow rate set for noncoincident type?
output: For noncoincident, the design system heating flow rate is set to be the larger of the airloop heating maximum flow rate sum and the design flow rate from the load based calculations.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the design system main flow rate determined?
output: The design system main flow rate is set to be the larger of the airloop maximum flow rate sum and the design flow rate from the larger of the cooling and heating calculations.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the cooling design air flow rate set for a cooling dominant air loop?
output: For cooling dominant, the cooling design air flow rate is set to the design main air flow, typically the airLoopMaxFlowRateSum.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the cooling design air flow rate set for a heating dominant air loop?
output: For heating dominant, the cooling design air flow rate is set to the larger of the original cooling-load-based value for flow and the lowest value the air handler will really operate at.

input: In EnergyPlus, why is the air terminal summation not as useful for coincident type sums?
output: The air terminal summation is not as useful because we generally expect that the straight sum of air terminal sizes will be larger than the coincident sum.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of adjustments made to keep design flows within bounds?
output: The adjustments are made to keep design flows within bounds set by minimum and maximum sums so that the coincident sum is within physical bounds set by how the air terminals can operate.

input: In EnergyPlus, for coincident and cooling dominant airloops, how is the heating design flow rate determined?
output: The heating design flow rate is the larger of the heating minimum flow rate and the design heat flow from the coincident design calculation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the main design flow treated in coincident and cooling dominant airloops?
output: The main design flow is not typically altered but will be checked to be at least as large as the heating minimum flow rate.

input: In EnergyPlus, what defines the cooling design flow rate for coincident and cooling dominant airloops?
output: The cooling design flow rate is set to the main design flow which is expected to be the result of the coincident design calculation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, for coincident and heating dominant airloops, how is the heating design flow rate determined?
output: The heating design flow rate is the larger of the heating maximum flow rate and the design heat flow rate from the coincident design calculation.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the basis for setting the main design flow rate in coincident and heating dominant airloops?
output: The main design flow rate is set to be the larger of the heating maximum flow rate and main design flow rate from the coincident sizing calculations.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the cooling design flow rate determined for coincident and heating dominant airloops?
output: The cooling design flow rate is set to be the larger of the heating minimum flow rate and the cooling design flow rate from the coincident calculation.

input: In EnergyPlus, where are the resulting adjusted system sizes for each airloop reported?
output: The resulting adjusted system sizes for each airloop are reported to the EIO and table summary report using the outputs 'Adjusted Heating Design Air Flow Rate [m3/s],' 'Adjusted Cooling Design Air Flow Rate [m3/s],' and 'Adjusted Main Design Air Flow Rate [m3/s].'

input: In EnergyPlus, what routine includes calculating the ratio for the central heating maximum system air flow rate?
output: The routine ManageSystemSizingAdjustments includes calculating the ratio for the central heating maximum system air flow rate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the input field called that represents the central heating maximum system air flow ratio?
output: The input field is called Central Heating Maximum System Air Flow Ratio in the Sizing:System object.

input: From EnergyPlus, as of which version can the central heating maximum system air flow ratio be autosized?
output: As of version 8.9, the central heating maximum system air flow ratio can be autosized.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens to the value of the central heating maximum system air flow ratio even if the input was not autosized?
output: The value is calculated even if the input was not autosized so that inputs can be checked.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how are the corrected values used in relation to the central heating flow ratio?
output: The corrected values are used to autosize the central heating flow ratio, if set to autosize by the user.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the central heating maximum system air flow ratio calculated?
output: The ratio is calculated by dividing the adjusted design heating flow by the adjusted design main flow.

input: In EnergyPlus, what object is used to set the design outdoor air flow rate to autosize?
output: The Sizing:System object is used to set the design outdoor air flow rate to autosize.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what methods can be chosen in the System Output Air Method field in Sizing:System for sizing calculations?
output: The methods that can be chosen are ZoneSum, Standard62.1VentilationRateProcedure, or Standard62.1SimplifiedProcedure.

input: In EnergyPlus, what do the sizing calculations for the system-level design outdoor air flow rate depend on?
output: The sizing calculations depend on the method chosen in the System Output Air Method field and the design results at the zone level.

input: According to EnergyPlus, which approach do the calculations generally follow for outdoor air flow rate sizing?
output: The calculations generally follow the Standard 62.1 approach.

input: In EnergyPlus, how are the sizing calculations applied for outdoor air flow rate during peak conditions?
output: The sizing calculations apply the Standard 62.1 calculations separately for both peak cooling design conditions and peak heating design conditions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the single design outdoor air volume flow rate determined?
output: The single design outdoor air volume flow rate is determined by taking the larger value from the peak cooling design conditions and peak heating design conditions.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the predefined table summary report 'Standard 62.1 Summary' provide?
output: The 'Standard 62.1 Summary' provides a comprehensive summary of the calculations for outdoor air rate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the basis for the system level summations and flow rate results as of version 8.9?
output: The system level summations and flow rate results are based on the adjusted system sizes and zone level summations that mine the individual air terminals attached to the air handlers.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does scalable system sizing apply to?
output: Scalable system sizing applies to system supply air flow rates and system capacity in cooling and heating modes.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the methods allowed for scalable system air flow sizing?
output: The methods allowed for scalable system air flow sizing are FlowPerFloorArea, FractionOfAutosizedCoolingAirflow, or FlowPerCoolingCapacity.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the cooling supply air volume flow rate calculated using FlowPerFloorArea?
output: The cooling supply air volume flow rate is calculated from zone floor area served by the airloop and user specified Flow Per Floor Area value.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does FractionOfAutosizedCoolingAirflow mean?
output: FractionOfAutosizedCoolingAirflow means the program calculates the cooling supply air volume flow rate from user specified fraction and the autosized design cooling supply air volume flow rate value determined by the simulation.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the heating supply air volume flow rate calculated using FractionOfAutosizedHeatingAirflow?
output: The heating supply air volume flow rate is calculated from user specified fraction and the autosized design heating supply air volume flow rate value determined by the simulation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the supply air volume calculated using FlowPerCoolingCapacity?
output: The supply air volume is calculated from user specified flow per cooling capacity and design cooling capacity determined by the simulation.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the supply air volume calculated using FlowPerHeatingCapacity?
output: The supply air volume is calculated from user specified flow per heating capacity and design heating capacity determined by the simulation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what scalable sizing methods are available for system capacity?
output: The scalable sizing methods for system capacity available are CapacityPerFloorArea, FractionOfAutosizedCoolingCapacity, and FractionOfAutosizedHeatingCapacity.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the design capacity calculated using CapacityPerFloorArea?
output: The design capacity is calculated from user specified capacity per floor area and floor area of the zones served by the airloop.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does FractionOfAutosizedCoolingCapacity mean?
output: FractionOfAutosizedCoolingCapacity means the program calculates the design cooling capacity from user specified fraction and the auto-sized design cooling capacity.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the design heating capacity calculated using FractionOfAutosizedHeatingCapacity?
output: The design heating capacity is calculated from user specified fraction and the auto-sized design heating capacity.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the focus of the section labeled 'Zone Design Loads and Air Flow Rates'?
output: The focus of the section is on Zone Design Loads and Air Flow Rates.

input: In EnergyPlus, what factors influence the method used to size an HVAC system?
output: Different building designs, climates, and HVAC systems impose varying constraints on the designer.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the method for sizing HVAC systems differ between climates?
output: The method used to size an HVAC system in a hot, moist climate such as Miami will be different than the method used for a building in Albuquerque.

input: In EnergyPlus, what type of load estimation might be adequate for a building containing a network server farm?
output: A simple watts per square foot loads estimate could be adequate for a building containing a network server farm.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what type of simulation is necessary for a passive solar building?
output: A detailed, dynamic loads simulation would be necessary for a passive solar building.

input: In EnergyPlus, what role does the designer's experience play in HVAC sizing calculations?
output: The designer's experience and engineering judgment will play an important role in any sizing calculation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what begins the HVAC equipment sizing process?
output: HVAC equipment sizing begins with the calculation of space heating and cooling sensible and/or latent loads.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is a space cooling sensible load defined?
output: A space cooling sensible load is defined as the rate at which heat must be removed to maintain a constant zone temperature.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is a space heating latent load defined?
output: A space heating latent load is defined as the rate at which moisture must be added to a space to maintain a constant zone moisture/humidity ratio/relative humidity level.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the current industry standard method for calculating space loads?
output: The current industry standard method for calculating space loads is the heat balance method.

input: According to EnergyPlus, why is it straightforward for the program to use the heat balance method?
output: Since EnergyPlus is a heat balance based simulation program, it is straightforward for the program to use this method for calculating zone loads.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does ZoneSizingInput(i) store?
output: ZoneSizingInput(i) stores the input data from the Sizing:Zone objects.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does CalcZoneSizing(i,j) represent?
output: CalcZoneSizing(i,j) stores the results of the zone design calculations for all zones and all design days.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of CalcFinalZoneSizing(i)?

input: From EnergyPlus, how does ZoneSizing(i,j) differ from CalcZoneSizing(i,j)?
output: ZoneSizing(i,j) corresponds to CalcZoneSizing but includes the effect of the user specified sizing factor or user specified zone design flow rate.

output: FinalZoneSizing(i) corresponds to CalcFinalZoneSizing but includes the effect of the user specified sizing factor or user specified zone design flow rate.
