input: What is the equation for the total cooling capacity at the lowest speed in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total cooling capacity at the lowest speed is calculated as \\( \\rm{Q}_{\\rm{total},1} = \\rm{Rated~Total~Cooling~Capacity} @ \\rm{Speed~Level} \\left( 1 \\right) \\rm{*} \\rm{TotCapTempModFa} \\rm{c}_1 \\rm{*TotCapAirFlowModFa} \\rm{c}_1 \\)

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) at the lowest speed in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) at the lowest speed is calculated as \\( \\rm{EI} \\rm{R}_1 = \\frac{1.0}{\\rm{Reference~Unit~COP} @ \\rm{Speed}(1)}{\\rm{EIRTempModFa}}{\\rm{c}_1}{\\rm{*EIRAirFlowModFa}}{\\rm{c}_1} \\)

input: What is the equation for the power consumption excluding the indoor fan at the lowest speed in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the power consumption excluding the indoor fan at the lowest speed is given by \\( \\rm{Powe}{{\rm{r}}_1} = {{\rm{Q}}_{{\rm{total}},1}}{\\rm{*EI}}{{\rm{R}}_1}{\\rm{*RTF}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the part load ratio (PLR) for sensible cooling in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part load ratio (PLR) for sensible cooling is calculated as \\( \\rm{PLR} = \\frac{\\rm{SensibleCoolingLoad}}{(\\rm{Q}_{\\rm{total},1}{\\rm{*SH}}{{\\rm{R}}_1})} \\)

input: What is the equation for the part load ratio (PLR) for latent cooling in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part load ratio (PLR) for latent cooling is given by \\( \\rm{PLR} = \\frac{\\rm{LatentCoolingLoad}}{[\\rm{Q}_{\\rm{total},1}{\\rm{*}}(1.0 - \\rm{SH}}{{\\rm{R}}_1)]} \\)

input: What is the equation for the design air flow rate at speed ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the design air flow rate at speed ratio is calculated as \\( \\rm{DesignAirFlowRateSpeedRatio} = \\rm{Reference~Unit~Air~Mass~Flow~Rate} @ \\rm{Speed~Level} \\left( \\rm{x} - 1 \\right) \\rm{*} \\rm{CapacityScaleFactor*} \\left( 1 - \\rm{SpeedRatio} \\right) + \\rm{Reference~Unit~Air~Mass~Flow~Rate} @ \\rm{Speed~Level} \\left( \\rm{x} \\right) \\rm{*} \\rm{CapacityScaleFactor*SpeedRatio} \\)

input: What is the equation for the total cooling capacity at speed x-1 in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total cooling capacity at speed x-1 is given by \\( \\rm{Q}_{\\rm{total},\\rm{x} - 1} = \\rm{Rated~Total~Cooling~Capacity} @ \\rm{Speed~Level} \\left( \\rm{x} - 1 \\right) \\rm{*} \\rm{TotCapTempModFa} \\rm{c}_{\\rm{x} - 1} \\rm{*TotCapAirFlowModFa} \\rm{c}_{\\rm{x} - 1} \\)

input: What is the equation for the total cooling capacity at speed x in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total cooling capacity at speed x is calculated as \\( \\rm{Q}_{\\rm{total},\\rm{x}} = \\rm{Rated~Total~Cooling~Capacity} @ \\rm{Speed~Level} \\left( \\rm{x} \\right) \\rm{*} \\rm{TotCapTempModFa} \\rm{c}_{\\rm{x}} \\rm{*TotCapAirFlowModFa} \\rm{c}_{\\rm{x}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) at speed x-1 in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) at speed x-1 is given by \\( \\rm{EI} \\rm{R}_{\\rm{x} - 1} = \\frac{1.0}{\\rm{Reference~Unit~COP}@\\rm{Speed}(\\rm{x} - 1)}{\\rm{EIRTempModFa}}{{\\rm{c}}_{\\rm{x} - 1}}{\\rm{*EIRAirFlowModFa}}{{\\rm{c}}_{\\rm{x} - 1}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) at speed x in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) at speed x is expressed as \\( \\rm{EI} \\rm{R}_{\\rm{x}} = \\frac{1.0}{\\rm{Reference~Unit~COP}@\\rm{Speed}\\left( \\rm{x} \\right)}{\\rm{EIRTempModFa}}{{\\rm{c}}_{\\rm{x}}}{\\rm{*EIRAirFlowModFa}}{{\\rm{c}}_{\\rm{x}}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the total cooling capacity at the corresponding speed ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total cooling capacity at the corresponding speed ratio is given by \\( {{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} = \\left( {1.0 - {\\rm{SpeedRatio}}} \\right){{\\rm{*}}{{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{x}} - 1}} + {\\rm{SpeedRatio*}}{{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{x}}}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the power consumption at the corresponding speed ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the power consumption at the corresponding speed ratio is calculated as \\( \\rm{Powe}{{\\rm{r}}_{{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} = \\left( {1.0 - {\\rm{SpeedRatio}}} \\right){{\\rm{*}}{{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{x}} - 1}}{\\rm{*EI}}{{\\rm{R}}_{{\\rm{x} - 1}} + {\\rm{SpeedRatio*}}{{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{x}}}}{\\rm{*EI}}{{\\rm{R}}_{\\rm{x}}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the net heat discharged from the condenser at the corresponding speed ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the net heat discharged from the condenser at the corresponding speed ratio is given by \\( {{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{cond}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} = {\\rm{Powe}}{{\\rm{r}}_{{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} + {{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the effective surface area in the correlations of BF factor at the corresponding speed ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the effective surface area in the correlations of BF factor at the corresponding speed ratio is calculated as \\( {{\\rm{A}}_{{\\rm{o}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} = \\left( {1 - {\\rm{SpeedRatio}}} \\right){{\\rm{*}}{{\\rm{A}}_{{\\rm{o}},{\\rm{x}} - 1}} + {\\rm{SpeedRatio*}}{{\\rm{A}}_{{\\rm{o}},{\\rm{x}}}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the sensible cooling capacity at the corresponding speed ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the sensible cooling capacity at the corresponding speed ratio is calculated as \\( {{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{sensible}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} = {{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}}{\\rm{*SH}}{{\\rm{R}}_{{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the sensible cooling capacity when matching the sensible cooling load in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, if the variable-speed DX cooling coil is used to match the sensible cooling load, then it is expressed as \\( {{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{sensible}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} = {\\rm{SensibleLoad}} \\)

input: What is the equation for the total cooling capacity when matching the latent cooling load in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, if it intends to match the latent cooling load, the equation is given by \\( {{\\rm{Q}}_{{\\rm{total}},{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}}{\\rm{*}}\\left( {1.0 - {\\rm{SH}}{{\\rm{R}}_{{\\rm{SpeedRatio}}}}} \\right) = {\\rm{LatentLoad}} \\)

input: In EnergyPlus, what must the user enter when using an evaporative pre-cooling pad upstream of the condenser?
output: The user must enter the appropriate evaporative effectiveness for the media at each compressor speed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the evaporative effectiveness correlated with compressor speed?
output: The evaporative effectiveness is correlated with compressor speed by interpolating between speed levels as a function of the condenser air flow rate.

input: From EnergyPlus, what formula is used to interpolate the evaporative effectiveness at the speed ratio?
output: The formula used is: Effectiveness{SpeedRatio} = (1.0 - SpeedRatio) * Effectiveness{x - 1} + SpeedRatio * Effectiveness{x}.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the air temperature reduction across the evaporative cooling pad calculated?
output: The air temperature reduction is calculated using the interpolated effectiveness at the speed ratio.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is used in place of the ambient temperature when calculating the decreased air temperature entering the condenser coil?
output: The decreased air temperature entering the condenser coil is calculated using the outdoor air wet bulb temperature and the evaporative effectiveness.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does T_{c,i} represent?
output: T_{c,i} represents the condenser entering air temperature in degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the outdoor air wet bulb and dry bulb temperatures represented by?
output: The outdoor air wet bulb temperature is represented by T_{wb,o} and the outdoor air dry bulb temperature is represented by T_{db,o}, both in degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the water consumption rate calculated?
output: The water consumption rate is calculated based on the interpolated condenser air flow rate at the speed ratio.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what formula is used to calculate the condenser flow rate at the speed ratio?
output: The formula used is: \dot m_{condair,SpeedRatio} = (1.0 - SpeedRatio) * \dot m_{condair,x - 1} + SpeedRatio * \dot m_{condair,x}.

input: In EnergyPlus, what industry standards are used for the standard rating of variable speed direct expansion cooling coils?
output: The industry standards used are ANSI/AHRI Standard 210-240 and ANSI/AHRI Standard 340-360.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what standard ratings are calculated and reported for variable speed direct expansion cooling coils?
output: The standard ratings calculated include Standard Rating Cooling Capacity, Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER), Integrated Energy Efficiency Ratio (IEER), and Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (SEER).

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the cooling capacity threshold for the AHRI Standard ratings to apply?
output: The AHRI Standard ratings apply only to air-to-air unitary heat pumps and air conditioners with rated cooling capacities less than 65,000 Btu/h (19,000 Watts).

input: In EnergyPlus, which version of the AHRI standard added support for the 2023 version?
output: Support for the 2023 version of the AHRI standard was added in EnergyPlus version 22.2.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what designations were updated in the 2023 version of the AHRI standard?
output: The updated Standard Ratings are designated as Standard Rating Cooling Capacity, Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER2), and Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (SEER2).

input: From EnergyPlus, what type of equipment does the AHRI Standard 340-360 apply to?
output: The AHRI Standard 340-360 applies to factory-made Commercial and Industrial Unitary Air-conditioning and Heat Pump Equipment with rated cooling/heating capacities greater than 65,000 Btu/h (19 kW) and less than 250,000 Btu/h (73.2 kW).

input: What is the equation used in EnergyPlus to interpolate the evaporative effectiveness as a function of compressor speed?
output: In EnergyPlus, the evaporative effectiveness is interpolated as {\rm{Effectivenes}}{{\rm{s}}_{{\rm{SpeedRatio}}}} = \left( {1.0 - {\rm{SpeedRatio}}} \right){\rm{*Effectivenes}}{{\rm{s}}_{{\rm{x}} - 1}} + {\rm{SpeedRatio*Effectivenes}}{{\rm{s}}_{\rm{x}}}

input: How is the decreased air temperature entering the condenser coil calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the decreased air temperature entering the condenser coil is calculated as {{\rm{T}}_{{\rm{c}},{\rm{i}}}} = {{\rm{T}}_{{\rm{wb}},{\rm{o}}}} + (1.0 - {\rm{Effectivenes}}{{\rm{s}}_{{\rm{SpeedRatio}}}}){\rm{*}}({{\rm{T}}_{{\rm{db}},{\rm{o}}}} - {{\rm{T}}_{{\rm{wb}},{\rm{o}}}})

input: What is the equation for calculating the condenser air flow rate at the speed ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the condenser air flow rate at the speed ratio is calculated as {\dot m_{condair,{\rm{}}SpeedRatio}} = \left( {1.0 - SpeedRatio} \right){\rm{*}}{\dot m_{condair,{\rm{}}x - 1}} + SpeedRatio{\rm{*}}{\dot m_{condair,{\rm{}}x}}

input: In EnergyPlus, where are the values for Standard Ratings reported?
output: The values for these Standard Ratings are reported in the eplusout.eio output file.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what predefined tabular output reports include Standard Ratings?
output: '2017 Standard Ratings for DX Coils' and '2023 Standard Ratings for DX Coils' are the predefined tabular output reports that include Standard Ratings.

input: In EnergyPlus, which object is used to generate summary reports that include Standard Ratings?
output: The Output:Table:SummaryReports object is used to generate summary reports that include Standard Ratings.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the object name for the electric air heating coil?
output: The object name for the electric air heating coil is Coil:Heating:Electric.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what type of model does the electric air heating coil use?
output: The electric air heating coil uses a simple capacity model.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the typical efficiency for the electric air heating coil?
output: In many cases, the efficiency for the electric coil will be 100%.

input: From EnergyPlus, what types of nodes does the electric air heating coil have to connect it in the system?
output: The coil only has air nodes to connect it in the system.

input: In EnergyPlus, where can the electric air heating coil be used?
output: The coil can be used in the air loop simulation or in the zone equipment as a reheat coil.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the electric air heating coil controlled when used in the air loop simulation?
output: When used in the air loop simulation, it will be controlled to a specified temperature on the setpoint node by the SetpointManager.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the electric air heating coil controlled when used in zone equipment?
output: When used in zone equipment, it will be controlled from the zone thermostat by meeting the zone demand.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if the zone demand exceeds the capacity of the electric air heating coil?
output: If the zone demand exceeds the capacity of the coil specified by the user, it will not be met.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the first condition checked in the simulation code for the electric air heating coil?
output: The first condition checked is if AirMassFlow is greater than 0.0 and HeatingCoil(CoilNum)%NominalCapacity is greater than 0.0.

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens if the required heating capacity exceeds the user-specified capacity in the electric air heating coil?
output: If the required heating capacity exceeds the user-specified capacity, QCoilCap will be set to HeatingCoil(CoilNum)%NominalCapacity.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the output temperature calculated for the electric air heating coil?
output: The output temperature is calculated as TempAirOut = TempAirIn + QCoilCap/CapacitanceAir.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does HeatingCoilLoad represent in the context of the electric air heating coil?
output: HeatingCoilLoad represents the change in the enthalpy of the Heating.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the electric usage load calculated for the electric air heating coil?
output: The electric usage load is calculated as HeatingCoil(CoilNum)%ElecUseLoad = HeatingCoilLoad/Effic.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the temperature setpoint coil in the electric air heating coil simulation?
output: The temperature setpoint coil controls the coil output to meet a setpoint temperature.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what condition is checked to determine if the coil output should be set to zero?
output: The condition checked is if QCoilCap is less than or equal to 0.0.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens if the calculated QCoilCap is greater than the nominal capacity of the electric air heating coil?
output: If QCoilCap is greater than HeatingCoil(CoilNum)%NominalCapacity, QCoilCap will be set to HeatingCoil(CoilNum)%NominalCapacity.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the output temperature when QCoilCap is less than or equal to zero?
output: When QCoilCap is less than or equal to zero, the output temperature is set to TempAirIn.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the output temperature when QCoilCap is less than the user-specified capacity?
output: When QCoilCap is less than the user-specified capacity, the output temperature is set to TempSetPoint.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the object name for the fuel-powered heating coil?
output: The object name for the fuel-powered heating coil is Coil:Heating:Fuel.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default burner efficiency for the fuel-powered heating coil?
output: The default for the burner efficiency is 80%.

input: In EnergyPlus, what types of nodes does the fuel-powered heating coil have?
output: The fuel-powered heating coil only has air nodes to connect it in the system.

input: From EnergyPlus, where can the fuel-powered heating coil be used?
output: The coil can be used in the air loop simulation or in the zone equipment as a reheat coil.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the control of the fuel-powered heating coil determined?
output: Depending on where it is used, the control of the coil is determined by whether it is temperature or capacity controlled.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the fuel-powered heating coil controlled when used in the air loop simulation?
output: When used in the air loop simulation, it will be controlled to a specified temperature scheduled from the SetpointManager.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the fuel-powered heating coil controlled when used in zone equipment?
output: When used in zone equipment, it will be controlled from the zone thermostat by meeting the zone demand.

input: From EnergyPlus, what additional features does the fuel-powered heating coil have?
output: The fuel coil has additional features that can add a part load correction and a parasitic fuel or electric load.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the parasitic electric load associated with the gas coil operation include?
output: The parasitic electric load associated with the gas coil operation includes elements such as an inducer fan.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the parasitic electric load modified during simulation?
output: The parasitic electric load is modified by the PLR (or coil runtime fraction if a part-load fraction correlation is provided) to reflect the time of operation in a simulation time step.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the assumption made about the parasitic fuel load associated with the gas coil's operation?
output: The model assumes that the parasitic fuel load is consumed only for the portion of the simulation time step where the gas heating coil is not operating.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the part load correction define?
output: The part load correction defines the name of a quadratic or cubic performance curve that parameterizes the variation of fuel consumption rate by the heating coil as a function of the part load ratio (PLR).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the nominal fuel consumption rate calculated for the heating coil?
output: The nominal fuel consumption rate is calculated by dividing the heating load by the burner efficiency.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if a part-load curve has been defined?
output: If a part-load curve has been defined, the nominal fuel consumption rate is divided by the part-load fraction (PLF).

input: In EnergyPlus, what should the part-load fraction correlation be normalized to when the part load ratio equals 1.0?
output: The part-load fraction correlation should be normalized to a value of 1.0 when the part load ratio equals 1.0.

input: From EnergyPlus, what rules apply for PLR values between 0 and 1?
output: For PLR values between 0 and 1, the rules are that PLF must be greater than or equal to 0.7 and PLF must be greater than or equal to PLR.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens if PLF is less than 0.7?
output: If PLF is less than 0.7, a warning message is issued, the program resets the PLF value to 0.7, and the simulation proceeds.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the runtime fraction of the heating coil defined?
output: The runtime fraction of the heating coil is defined as PLR/PLF.

input: In EnergyPlus, what occurs if PLF is less than PLR?
output: If PLF is less than PLR, then a warning message is issued and the runtime fraction of the coil is limited to 1.0.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is a typical part load fraction correlation for a conventional gas heating coil?
output: A typical part load fraction correlation for a conventional gas heating coil is PLF = 0.8 + 0.2·PLR.

input: In EnergyPlus, where can additional information regarding how the coil meets temperature setpoints be found?
output: Additional information regarding how the coil meets temperature setpoints can be found in Coil:Electric:Heating.

input: According to EnergyPlus, where can more input information be referenced?
output: More input information can be referenced in the Input Output Reference.

input: What is the equation for the part-load fraction (PLF) in EnergyPlus for a conventional gas heating coil?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part-load fraction is defined as PLF = 0.8 + 0.2\cdot PLR.

input: In EnergyPlus, what object names are used to simulate the performance of multi-stage electric and gas heating systems?
output: The object names are Coil:Heating:Electric:MultiStage and Coil:Heating:Gas:MultiStage.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how many discrete air flow stages can the multi-stage heating systems simulate?
output: The multi-stage heating systems can simulate two to four discrete air flow stages.

input: In EnergyPlus, what parameters are user inputted for each stage of the multi-stage heating systems?
output: User inputted parameters include gas burner efficiency, nominal capacity, and parasitic electric load (for gas coil only).

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the full load supply airflow rate determined for the multi-stage heating systems?
output: The full load supply airflow rate is dependent on the stage number and is set by its parent object, which is AirLoopHVAC:UnitaryHeatPump:AirToAir:MultiSpeed.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the part-load impact on coil energy use get applied?
output: The part-load impact on coil energy use is automatically applied to the lowest stage.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the performance of the model at Stage 1 compare to the Coil:Heating:Electric and Coil:Heating:Fuel models?
output: The performance at Stage 1 or cycling between OFF and Stage 1 is almost the same as the performance for the Coil:Heating:Electric and Coil:Heating:Fuel models.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the multistage coil model determine performance at higher stages?
output: The multistage coil model linearly interpolates the performance at two consecutive stages (n-1 and n) as needed to meet the heating load.

input: From EnergyPlus, what determines the fraction of time at each speed for the multistage coil model?
output: The fraction of time at each speed is established by the speed ratio.

input: In EnergyPlus, what parent object can call the multistage coil model?
output: The multistage coil model can only be called by the parent object AirLoopHVAC:UnitaryHeatPump:AirToAir:MultiSpeed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the main difference between the multistage model and the Coil:Heating:Electric and Coil:Heating:Fuel objects?
output: The main difference is that the multistage model requires a set of fields at each speed, such as nominal capacity and efficiency.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the total delivered heating capacity for Stage 1 calculated?
output: The total delivered heating capacity for Stage 1 is calculated using the equation Q_{coil,cycling} = {\dot{m}_{Speed~1}} (CycRatio) (h_{inlet} - h_{outlet,full}).

input: From EnergyPlus, what does Q_{coil,cycling} represent?
output: Q_{coil,cycling} represents the delivered sensible heating capacity for Stage 1 operating at a specific cycling ratio.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the significance of CycRatio in the calculation of heating capacity?
output: CycRatio is the cycling ratio at Stage 1, which is the ratio of requested heating load to the full-load capacity of the coil at Stage 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the average specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air calculated?
output: The average specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air is calculated based on the delivered sensible heating capacity and the average air mass flow rate entering the coil.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the equation used to calculate the average specific enthalpy at the coil outlet?
output: The equation is h_{outlet,average} = h_{inlet} - \frac{Q_{coil,cycling}}{{\mathop m\limits^\cdot }_{inlet}}.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does h_{outlet,average} represent?
output: h_{outlet,average} represents the average specific enthalpy at the coil outlet.

input: From EnergyPlus, how does the heating coil affect the outlet air humidity ratio?
output: The heating coil's outlet air humidity ratio equals the inlet air humidity ratio since the coil does not change the moisture content of the air.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the average outlet air temperature calculated?
output: The average outlet air temperature is calculated based on the inlet air humidity ratio and the average outlet air enthalpy using the psychrometric function PsyTdbFnHW.

input: What is the equation for the total delivered heating capacity for Stage 1 operating at the cycling ratio needed to meet the requested heating load in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total delivered heating capacity for Stage 1 is calculated as Q_{coil,cycling} = {\dot{m}_{Speed~1}} \left( CycRatio \right) (h_{inlet} - h_{outlet,full})

input: How is the average specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the average specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air is calculated as h_{outlet,average} = h_{inlet} - \frac{Q_{coil,cycling}}{{\mathop m\limits^\cdot }_{inlet}}

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the main reason for using the approach described in the text?
output: The main reason for using the above approach is that outlet air conditions are calculated in the same way for all operating Stages.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what calculations are performed when the required sensible load is less than the full load sensible capacity at Stage n?
output: Total delivered heating capacity at Stage n-1 and Stage n is calculated.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the total delivered heating capacity at Stage n-1 calculated?
output: TotCap_{n - 1} = MSNominalCap_{n - 1}.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the total delivered heating capacity at Stage n calculated?
output: TotCap_n = MSNominalCap_n.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does TotCap_i represent?
output: TotCap_i is the total delivered heating capacity at given temperatures and flow rates at Stage i (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does MSNominalCap_i represent?
output: MSNominalCap_i is the heating capacity at the rated conditions at Stage i (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the full load outlet air specific enthalpy at Stage n calculated?
output: h_{outlet,full~Speed~n} = h_{inlet} - (MSNominalCap_n/{\dot{m}_{inlet}}).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the full load outlet air specific enthalpy at Stage n-1 calculated?
output: h_{outlet,full~Speed~n-1} = h_{inlet} - (MSNominalCap_{n - 1}/{\dot{m}_{inlet}}).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does h_{outlet,full~Speed~n} represent?
output: h_{outlet,full~Speed~n} is the specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air during full-load operation at Stage n (no cycling) (J/kg).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does h_{outlet,full~Speed~n-1} represent?

input: In EnergyPlus, what object name simulates the performance of an air-to-air direct expansion heating system?
output: The object name is Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what factors are used to determine the performance of the DX heating system at part-load conditions?
output: Performance information at rated conditions along with curve fits for variations in total capacity, energy input ratio, and part-load fraction are used.

input: In EnergyPlus, what adjustment factors are applied to account for frost formation on the outdoor coil?
output: Adjustment factors are applied to total capacity and input power.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is considered the rating condition for the outdoor air temperature?

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the recommended range for the rated volumetric air flow across the DX heating coil?
output: The rated volumetric air flow should be between 0.00004027 m³/s and 0.00006041 m³/s per watt of rated total heating capacity.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is a recommended curve type for the total heating capacity modifier curve based on temperature?
output: A bi-quadratic curve is recommended if sufficient manufacturer data is available.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the total heating capacity at specific temperature operating conditions calculated?

output: TotCapTempModFac = a + b(T_{db,o}) + c(T_{db,o})².

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the independent variable for the total heating capacity modifier curve based on flow fraction?

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve function of temperature depend on?

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the EIR at specific temperature operating conditions calculated?
output: The output of the EIR modifier curve is multiplied by the rated EIR.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the formula for the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve based on temperature?
output: EIRTempModFac = a + b(T_{db,o}) + c(T_{db,o})².

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the part-load fraction correlation based on part-load ratio?
output: The part-load fraction correlation is a quadratic or cubic curve with the independent variable being part-load ratio.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens if the part-load fraction (PLF) is less than 0.7?
output: A warning message is issued, and the program resets the PLF value to 0.7.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the formula for the part-load fraction correlation?
output: PartLoadFrac = PLF = a + b(PLR) + c(PLR)².

output: Adjustment factors to total heating coil capacity and input power are calculated.

input: What is the equation for the total heating capacity modifier curve as a cubic function of flow fraction in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total heating capacity modifier curve as a cubic function of flow fraction is given by TotCapFlowModFac = a + b( {ff} ) + c{( {ff} )^2} + d{( {ff} )^3}

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a function of temperature in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a function of temperature is given by EIRTempModFac = a + b( {T_{db,o}} ) + c{( {T_{db,o}} )^2}

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a cubic function of temperature in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a cubic function of temperature is given by EIRTempModFac = a + b( {T_{db,o}} ) + c{( {T_{db,o}} )^2} + d{( {T_{db,o}} )^3}

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a bi-quadratic function of indoor and outdoor air temperatures in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a bi-quadratic function is given by EIRTempModFac = a + b( {T_{db,i}} ) + c{( {T_{db,i}} )^2} + d( {T_{db,o}} ) + e{( {T_{db,o}} )^2} + f( {T_{db,i}} )( {T_{db,o}} )

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a function of flow fraction in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a function of flow fraction is given by EIRFlowModFac = a + b( {ff} ) + c{( {ff} )^2}

input: What is the equation for the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a cubic function of flow fraction in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the energy input ratio (EIR) modifier curve as a cubic function of flow fraction is given by EIRFlowModFac = a + b( {ff} ) + c{( {ff} )^2} + d{( {ff} )^3}

input: What is the equation for the part-load fraction correlation as a function of part-load ratio in EnergyPlus?

input: What is the equation for the part-load fraction correlation as a cubic function of part-load ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part-load fraction correlation as a cubic function of part-load ratio is given by PartLoadFrac = a + b( {PLR} ) + c{( {PLR} )^2} + d{( {PLR} )^3}

input: What is the equation for the part-load ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part-load ratio is defined as PLR = part-load~ratio = ( {sensible~heating~load} / {steady-state~heating~capacity} )

input: What is the equation for the outdoor coil temperature in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the outdoor coil temperature is calculated as {T_{coil,out}} = 0.82{T_{db,o}} - 8.589

input: What is the equation for the difference in outdoor air humidity ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the difference in outdoor air humidity ratio is calculated as \\Delta {\\omega_{\,coil,out}}\, = \,MAX[ {1.0E - 6,\,\,\,{\\omega_{outdoor}}\, - \,\,{\\omega_{sat}}( {{T_{coil,out}}\,,{\\rm{OutBaroPress}}} )} ]

input: What is the equation for the fractional defrost time for timed defrost in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, for timed defrost, the fractional defrost time is given by Fractional~Defrost~Time = time~period~specified~by~user = {t_{frac,defrost}}

input: What is the equation for the heating capacity multiplier for timed defrost in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the heating capacity multiplier for timed defrost is given by Heating~Capacity~Multiplier = 0.909 - 107.33( {\\Delta {\\omega_{\,coil,out}} } )

input: What is the equation for the input power multiplier for timed defrost in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the input power multiplier for timed defrost is given by Input~Power~Multiplier = 0.9 - 36.45( {\\Delta {\\omega_{\,coil,out}} } )

input: What is the equation for the fractional defrost time for on-demand defrost in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, for on-demand defrost, the fractional defrost time is given by Fractional~Defrost~Time = \\frac{1}{{1 + \\left( {\\frac{{0.01446}}{{\\Delta {\\omega_{\,coil,out}}}} \\right)}} = {t_{frac,defrost}}

input: What is the equation for the heating capacity multiplier for on-demand defrost in EnergyPlus?

input: What is the equation for the input power multiplier for on-demand defrost in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the input power multiplier for on-demand defrost is given by Input~Power~Multiplier = 0.954( {1 - {t_{frac,defrost}} } )

input: What is the equation for the additional indoor heating load during reverse-cycle defrost in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the additional indoor heating load during reverse-cycle defrost is given by {Q_{defrost}} = 0.01( {t_{frac,defrost}} )( {7.222 - {T_{db,o}}} )( {\\frac{{{Q_{total,rated}}}{{1.01667}}} )

input: What is the equation for the average defrost power during reverse-cycle defrost in EnergyPlus?

input: What is the equation for the additional indoor heating load during resistive defrost in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the additional indoor heating load during resistive defrost is given by {Q_{defrost}} = 0.0

input: What is the equation for the total heating capacity of the DX unit in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total heating capacity of the DX unit is calculated as Q_{total} = Q_{total,rated}( {TotCapTempModFac} )( {TotCapFlowModFac} )

input: What is the equation for adjusting the total heating capacity due to outdoor coil frost formation in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total heating capacity adjusted due to outdoor coil frost formation is given by Q_{total} = Q_{total}( {HeatingCapacityMultiplier} )

input: What is the equation for calculating the part-load ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part-load ratio is calculated as PLR = MIN ( 1.0,~PLR + ( {\\frac{Q_{defrost}}{Q_{total}} } ) )

input: What is the equation for calculating the part-load fraction in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part-load fraction is calculated as PartLoadFrac = a + b( {PLR} ) + c{( {PLR} )^2} + d{( {PLR} )^3}

input: What is the equation for calculating the heating power in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the heating power is calculated as P_{heating} = \\frac{{( {Q_{total}} )( {EIR} )( {PLR} )}}{{PartLoadFrac}} \\times InputPowerMultiplier

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \({P_{heating}}\) represent?
output: \({P_{heating}}\) is the average compressor and outdoor fan power for the simulation time step (W).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does \({Q_{total}}\) signify?
output: \({Q_{total}}\) is the total heating capacity from Equation~\\ref{eq:SSEHPDXHeatingCoilQtotal2} (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Energy Input Ratio (EIR) calculated?
output: EIR = Energy~Input~Ratio = \\left( \\frac{1}{{CO{P_{rated}}}} \\right)\\left( {EIRTempModFac} \\right)\\left( {EIRFlowModFac} \\right).

input: From EnergyPlus, what does \({CO{P_{rated}}}\) refer to?
output: \({CO{P_{rated}}}\) is the coefficient of performance at rated conditions (user input).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the \emph{InputPowerMultiplier}?
output: \emph{InputPowerMultiplier} is the power adjustment due to frost if applicable as in Equation~\\ref{eq:SSEHPDXInputPowerMultiplierTimedDefrost} or~\\ref{eq:SSEHPDXInputPowerMultiplierOnDemandDefrost}.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when does the crankcase heater operate?
output: The crankcase heater is assumed to operate when the heating coil's compressor is OFF.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the average crankcase heater power for the simulation time step calculated?
output: {P_{crankcase}} = {Q_{cap,crankcase}}\\left( {1 - RTF} \\right).

input: From EnergyPlus, what does \({P_{crankcase}}\) represent?
output: \({P_{crankcase}}\) is the average crankcase heater power for the simulation time step (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is RTF defined?
output: RTF = \\left( \\frac{PLR}{PartLoadFrac} \\right) = runtime~fraction~of~the~heating~coil.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is \({Q_{cap,crankcase}}\)?
output: \({Q_{cap,crankcase}}\) is the crankcase heater capacity (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the enthalpy of the air leaving the heating coil at full-load operation calculated?
output: The enthalpy is calculated using the equation: \\( h_{outlet} = h_{inlet} + \\frac{Q_{total}}{\\dot{m}} \\).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does \({h_{outlet}}\) signify?
output: \({h_{outlet}}\) is the enthalpy of the air leaving the heating coil (J/kg).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the humidity ratio of the leaving air represented by?
output: \({\\omega_{outlet}}\\) is the leaving air humidity ratio (kg/kg).

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the leaving air dry-bulb temperature calculated?
output: {T_{db,outlet}} = PsyTdbFnHW({h_{outlet}},{\\omega_{outlet}}).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the function \emph{PsyTdbFnHW} used for?
output: \emph{PsyTdbFnHW} is an EnergyPlus psychrometric function that returns dry-bulb temp given enthalpy and humidity ratio.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the air temperature entering the outdoor condenser determined?
output: The air temperature entering the outdoor condenser is based on the weather data used during a simulation.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens if the input for Condenser Air Inlet Node Name in the DX cooling coil object is left blank?
output: If left blank, the air temperature entering the condenser is based solely on the weather data.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is required if the Condenser Air Inlet Node Name is not blank?
output: The node name specified must also be listed in an OutdoorAir:Node or OutdoorAir:NodeList object.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the height of the node affect the air temperature entering the outdoor condenser?
output: When the node name is listed in an OutdoorAir:Node object, the height of the node determines the air temperature entering the outdoor condenser.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the two supply air fan operation modes available in the DX coil model?
output: The two operation modes are cycling fan, cycling compressor (CyclingFanAndCompressor) and continuous fan, cycling compressor (ContinuousFanWithCyclingCompressor).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is referred to as 'AUTO fan'?
output: The first operation mode, where the compressor(s) and supply air fan operate in unison to meet the zone heating load and cycle off together when the heating load has been met.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the 'fan ON' operation mode?
output: In the 'fan ON' operation mode, the compressor(s) cycle on and off to meet the zone heating load but the supply air fan operates continuously regardless of compressor operation.

input: What is the equation for the Energy Input Ratio (EIR) in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the Energy Input Ratio (EIR) is given by EIR = Energy~Input~Ratio = \\left( \\frac{1}{{CO{P_{rated}}}} \\right)\\left( {EIRTempModFac} \\right)\\left( {EIRFlowModFac} \\right)

input: How is the average crankcase heater power calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the average crankcase heater power is calculated as {P_{crankcase}} = {Q_{cap,crankcase}}\\left( {1 - RTF} \\right)

input: What is the equation for the runtime fraction (RTF) in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the runtime fraction (RTF) is defined as RTF = \\left( \\frac{PLR}{PartLoadFrac} \\right)

input: What is the equation used to calculate the enthalpy of the air leaving the heating coil in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the enthalpy of the air leaving the heating coil is calculated using the equation h_{outlet} = h_{inlet} + \\frac{Q_{total}}{\\dot{m}}

input: What is the equation for the leaving air humidity ratio in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the leaving air humidity ratio is given by {\\omega_{outlet}} = {\\omega_{inlet}}

input: How is the leaving air dry-bulb temperature calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the leaving air dry-bulb temperature is calculated as {T_{db,outlet}} = PsyTdbFnHW({h_{outlet}},{\\omega_{outlet}})

input: In EnergyPlus, what is required for a DX heating coil to be used?
output: The DX heating coil can only be used in conjunction with a DX cooling coil.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what determines the fan operation mode for each time step throughout the simulation when using a DX heating coil?
output: The fan operation mode schedule value determines the fan operation mode for each time step.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does a fan operation mode schedule value of 0 specify?
output: A fan operation mode schedule value of 0 specifies AUTO fan mode operation.

input: From EnergyPlus, how can the fan operation mode change based on time?
output: The use of a schedule allows the fan operation mode to change based on time-of-day or with changes in season.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the impact of HVAC equipment on an air stream determined?
output: The impact is determined by calculating the mass flow rate and air properties exiting the equipment.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what conditions are passed along as inlet conditions to the next component model in the air stream?
output: The exiting conditions, including mass flow rate and air properties such as enthalpy, dry-bulb temperature, and humidity ratio, are passed along.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is used in the zone energy balance to determine the resulting zone air temperature and humidity ratio?
output: The flow rate and properties of the air being supplied to the conditioned zone are used in the zone energy balance.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the air mass flow rate and air properties determined for cycling fan/cycling compressor mode?
output: The steady-state values calculated using specific equations are used for the air leaving the heating coil.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the average air mass flow rate determined for the system simulation time step?
output: It is determined by the heating system.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is passed to Fan:OnOff to properly calculate the supply air fan power?
output: The heating coil part-load fraction is passed to Fan:OnOff.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the air mass flow rate characterized for continuous fan/cycling compressor mode?
output: The air mass flow rate is constant for continuous fan/cycling compressor mode.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how are the air properties leaving the heating coil calculated for continuous fan/cycling compressor mode?
output: The air properties are calculated as the average conditions during the system simulation time step.

input: In EnergyPlus, what assumption is made about the air exiting the DX coil for the remainder of the system simulation time step?
output: It is assumed that the air exiting the DX coil has the same properties as the air entering the coil.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the leaving air property for continuous fan/cycling compressor calculated?
output: The leaving air property is calculated using specific equations based on the part-load ratio.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the equation to calculate the outlet enthalpy for continuous fan/cycling compressor?
output: The equation is {h_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}} = {h_{outlet}}(PLR) + {h_{inlet}}(1 - PLR).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the outlet humidity ratio for continuous fan/cycling compressor calculated?
output: It is calculated using the equation {\omega_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}} = {\omega_{outlet}}(PLR) + {\omega_{inlet}}(1 - PLR).

input: In EnergyPlus, what function is used to calculate the outlet dry-bulb temperature for continuous fan/cycling compressor?
output: The function used is PsyTdbFnHW({h_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}},{\omega_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}}).

input: What is the equation used in EnergyPlus to calculate the outlet enthalpy for continuous fan and cycling compressor?
output: In EnergyPlus, the outlet enthalpy is calculated as {h_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}} = {h_{outlet}}\left( {PLR} \right) + {h_{inlet}}\left( {1 - PLR} \right)

input: What is the equation used in EnergyPlus to calculate the outlet humidity ratio for continuous fan and cycling compressor?
output: In EnergyPlus, the outlet humidity ratio is calculated as {\omega_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}} = {\omega_{outlet}}\left( {PLR} \right) + {\omega_{inlet}}\left( {1 - PLR} \right)

input: What is the equation used in EnergyPlus to calculate the outlet dry-bulb temperature for continuous fan and cycling compressor?
output: In EnergyPlus, the outlet dry-bulb temperature is calculated as {T_{db,outlet,ContFanCycComp}} = PsyTdbFnHW({h_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}},{\omega_{outlet,ContFanCycComp}})

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the industry standard ratings for single-speed direct expansion heating coils based on?
output: The industry standard ratings are calculated according to the ANSI/AHRI Standard 210-240 (AHRI 2008/AHRI 2017).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the three standard ratings for single-speed direct expansion heating coils?
output: The three standard ratings are High Temperature Heating Standard (Net) Rating Capacity, Low Temperature Heating Standard (Net) Rating Capacity, and Heating Seasonal Performance Factor (HSPF).

input: In EnergyPlus, is the rated Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER) calculated for any DX heating coils?
output: The rated Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER) is not calculated for any DX heating coils at this time.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how are the standard ratings for the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed object determined?
output: These standard ratings are not direct inputs to the model but can be calculated using user-entered data for the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed object.

input: In EnergyPlus, where are the standard rating values for DX heating coils provided?
output: The standard rating values are provided in the eplusout.eio output file and in the predefined tabular output reports (Output:Table:SummaryReports object, Equipment Summary).

input: According to EnergyPlus, which versions of DX heating coils are standard ratings currently calculated for?
output: The standard ratings for DX heating coils are only calculated and output for single-speed and multi-speed DX heating coils.

input: In EnergyPlus, what version introduced support for newer standard ratings?
output: Support for newer version of these Standard Ratings was added in EnergyPlus version 22.2.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when were the new Standard Ratings introduced?
output: The new Standard Ratings were introduced in the 2023 version of the ANSI/AHRI Standard 210/240 (AHRI 2023).

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the designated new Standard Ratings?
output: The new Standard Ratings are designated as High Temperature Heating Standard (Net) Rating Capacity, Low Temperature Heating Standard (Net) Rating Capacity, and Heating Seasonal Performance Factor (HSPF2).

input: According to EnergyPlus, where can one find the equations used for the implementation of standard ratings?
output: The equations used in this implementation are detailed in ANSI/AHRI Standard 210/240 (Section 11.2.2.1).

input: In EnergyPlus, what conditions must be met for the standard ratings of DX heating coils to be evaluated?
output: The DX heating coil model must be evaluated at specific operating conditions, including specific temperatures for air entering the heating coil and for air entering the air-cooled outdoor condenser.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if the heating coil performance curves cannot be evaluated at the required test conditions?
output: A standard rating value will be calculated at user specified curve limit as an output, and a warning message will be written to eplusout.err.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the formula for calculating the Standard Rating Heating Capacity?
output: The formula is {\dot Q_{HighStandardRating}} = {\dot Q_{total,Rated}}\left( {TotCapTempModFa{c_{Rated}}} \right).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the total standard (net) heating capacity calculated?
output: The total standard (net) heating capacity is calculated using the formula {\dot Q_{HighStandardRating,Net}} = {\dot Q_{HighStandardRating}} + Fa{n_{Power,Rated}}.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the total standard heating capacity (W) determined from, according to the ANSI/AHRI Standard 210/240?
output: The total standard heating capacity is determined from ANSI/AHRI Standard 210/240 and specific test conditions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the standard heating test conditions for air-cooled condensers?
output: The standard heating test conditions for air-cooled condensers are: indoor coil entering air dry-bulb 21.1°C and outdoor coil entering air dry-bulb 8.33°C.

input: What is the equation for calculating the High Temperature Heating Standard Rating in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the High Temperature Heating Standard Rating is calculated as \\( \\dot Q_{HighStandardRating} = \\dot Q_{total,Rated}\\left( TotCapTempModFa{c_{Rated}} \\right) \\)

input: How is the High Temperature Heating Standard (Net) Rating Capacity calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the High Temperature Heating Standard (Net) Rating Capacity is calculated as \\( \\dot Q_{HighStandardRating,Net} = \\dot Q_{HighStandardRating} + Fa{n_{Power,Rated}} \\)

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \({\dot Q_{total,Rated}}\) represent?
output: \({\dot Q_{total,Rated}}\) is the rated total heating capacity, user input (W).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is \(TotCapTempModFa{c_{Rated}}\) evaluated at?
output: \(TotCapTempModFa{c_{Rated}}\) is evaluated at the indoor coil entering air dry-bulb 21.1\(^{\circ}\)C and outdoor coil entering air dry-bulb 8.33\(^{\circ}\)C for air-cooled condenser.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is \(Fa{n_{Power,Rated}}\)?
output: \(Fa{n_{Power,Rated}}\) is the supply air fan power at rated conditions, (W).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Rated Indoor Coil Fan Power Per Volume Flow rate if left blank by the user?
output: The default value is 773.3 W/(m\(^3\)/s).

input: In EnergyPlus, what standard is the default value for fan power taken from?
output: The default value is taken from ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 210/240-2008.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Low Temperature Standard Rating Heating Capacity calculated?
output: The Low Temperature Standard Rating Heating Capacity is calculated using the equation \({\dot Q_{LowStandardRating}} = {\dot Q_{total,Rated}}\left( {TotCapTempModFa{c_{H3Test}}} \right).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \({\dot Q_{LowStandardRating,Net}}\) represent?
output: \({\dot Q_{LowStandardRating,Net}}\) is the total standard (net) heating capacity (W) of the air-source heat pump equipment in heating mode.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the standard heating test conditions for air-cooled condenser?
output: The standard heating test conditions for air-cooled condenser are: indoor coil entering air dry-bulb 21.1\(^{\circ}\)C and outdoor coil entering air dry-bulb -8.33\(^{\circ}\)C.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the definition of Heating Seasonal Performance Factor (HSPF)?
output: HSPF is defined as the total space heating required during the space heating season, divided by the total electrical energy consumed by the heat pump system during the same season.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is HSPF calculated for a heat pump with a single-speed compressor?
output: HSPF is calculated using the equation \(HSPF = \frac{{\sum\limits_j^J {\left[ {\frac{{{n_j}}}{N} \cdot BL({T_j})} \right]} }}{{\sum\limits_j^J {\left[ {\frac{{{e_h}({T_j})}}{N}} \right]}  + \sum\limits_j^J {\left[ {\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}} \right]} }} \cdot {F_{def}}.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \(\frac{{{e_h}({T_j})}}{N}\) represent?
output: \(\frac{{{e_h}({T_j})}}{N}\) is the ratio of the electrical energy consumed by the heat pump during periods of the space heating season when the outdoor temperature fell within the range represented by bin temperature \({T_j}\) to the total number of hours (N) in the heating season.

input: What is the equation for calculating the Low Temperature Standard Rating Heating Capacity in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the Low Temperature Standard Rating Heating Capacity is calculated as \\(\\dot Q_{LowStandardRating} = \\dot Q_{total,Rated}\\left( TotCapTempModFac_{H3Test} \\right)\\)

input: How is the total standard (net) heating capacity calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the total standard (net) heating capacity is calculated as \\(\\dot Q_{LowStandardRating,Net} = \\dot Q_{LowStandardRating} + Fan_{Power,\,Rated}\\)

input: What is the formula for calculating the Heating Seasonal Performance Factor (HSPF) in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the Heating Seasonal Performance Factor (HSPF) is defined as \\(HSPF = \\frac{{\\sum\\limits_j^J {\\left[ \\frac{{n_j}}{N} \\cdot BL({T_j}) \\right]}}}{{\\sum\\limits_j^J {\\left[ \\frac{{e_h({T_j})}}{N} \\right]} + \\sum\\limits_j^J {\\left[ \\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N} \\right]} }} \\cdot F_{def}\\)

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \(\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}\) represent?
output: It represents the ratio of the electrical energy used for resistive space heating during periods when the outdoor temperature fell within the range represented by bin temperature \({T_j}\) to the total number of hours (N) in the heating season.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is \({T_j}\)?
output: \({T_j}\) is the outdoor bin temperature measured in degrees Celsius (°C).

input: In EnergyPlus, how are outdoor temperatures categorized for calculations?
output: Outdoor temperatures are 'binned' such that calculations are only performed based on one temperature within the bin, with bins of 2.78°C used.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does \(\frac{{{n_j}}}{N}\) represent?
output: \(\frac{{{n_j}}}{N}\) is the fractional bin hours for the heating season; it is the ratio of the number of hours during the heating season when the outdoor temperature fell within the range represented by bin temperature \({T_j}\) to the total number of hours in the heating season.

input: In EnergyPlus, where can \(\frac{{{n_j}}}{N}\) values be obtained?
output: \(\frac{{{n_j}}}{N}\) values can be obtained from Table 17 of AHRI Std. 210/240-2008.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does \(j\) represent?
output: \(j\) is the bin number, which is dimensionless.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \(J\) represent?
output: \(J\) is the total number of temperature bins for each generalized climatic region, which is dimensionless.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the demand defrost credit \({F_{def}}\)?
output: \({F_{def}}\) is the demand defrost credit described in section 3.9.2 of AHRI Std. 210/240-2008.

input: In EnergyPlus, what value is assigned to \({F_{def}}\) for timed defrost control?
output: For timed defrost control, a value of 1 is assigned to \({F_{def}}\).

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the building space conditioning load \(BL({T_j})\) defined?
output: \(BL({T_j})\) is the building space conditioning load corresponding to an outdoor temperature of \({T_j}\), depending on the generalized climatic region's outdoor design temperature and the design heating requirement.

input: In EnergyPlus, how can building heating load be evaluated?
output: Building heating load can be evaluated using the equation: \(BL({T_j}) = \frac{{\left( {18.33 - {T_j}} \right)}}{{\left( {18.33 - {T_{OD}}} \right)}} \cdot C \cdot DHR\).

input: From EnergyPlus, what is \(T_{OD}\)?
output: \(T_{OD}\) is the outdoor design temperature measured in degrees Celsius (°C).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the correction factor \(C\)?
output: The correction factor \(C\) is 0.77, which tends to improve the agreement between calculated and measured building loads.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does \(DHR\) represent?
output: \(DHR\) is the Design Heating Requirement, which is the amount of heating required to maintain a given indoor temperature at a particular outdoor design temperature.

input: In EnergyPlus, how can the minimum design heating requirement \(DHR_{min}\) be calculated?
output: The minimum design heating requirement \(DHR_{min}\) can be calculated using the specified equations for different regions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how can the maximum design heating requirement \(DHR_{max}\) be calculated?
output: The maximum design heating requirement \(DHR_{max}\) can be calculated using the specified equations for different regions.

input: In EnergyPlus, how should both \(DHR_{min}\) and \(DHR_{max}\) be treated after calculation?
output: Both \(DHR_{min}\) and \(DHR_{max}\) should be rounded to the nearest standardized DHR given in the relevant table.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does \(\frac{{{e_h}({T_j})}}{N}\) represent?
output: \(\frac{{{e_h}({T_j})}}{N}\) represents a calculated value based on the heating mode load factor and other parameters.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \(\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}\) represent in relation to building loads?
output: \(\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}\) is calculated based on the building load minus the heating capacity of the heat pump.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is \(X({T_j})\) defined?
output: In EnergyPlus, \(X({T_j})\) is defined as the minimum of either the ratio of building load to space heating capacity or 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is \(\mathop {{Q_h}}\limits^ \cdot ({T_j})\)?
output: \(\mathop {{Q_h}}\limits^ \cdot ({T_j})\) is the space heating capacity of the heat pump when operating at outdoor temperature \({T_j}\).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is \(\mathop {{E_h}}\limits^ \cdot ({T_j})\)?
output: \(\mathop {{E_h}}\limits^ \cdot ({T_j})\) is the electrical power consumption of the heat pump when operating at outdoor temperature \({T_j}\).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \(\delta ({T_j})\) represent?
output: \(\delta ({T_j})\) is the heat pump low temperature cut-out factor.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the part load factor \(PL{F_j}\) calculated?
output: The part load factor \(PL{F_j}\) is calculated using the equation \(PL{F_j} = 1 - {C_{{D^h}}}[1 - X({T_j})]\).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value of the degradation coefficient \({C_{{D^h}}}\)?
output: The default value of the degradation coefficient \({C_{{D^h}}}\) is 0.25.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the low temperature cut-out factor \(\delta ({T_j})\) determined?
output: The low temperature cut-out factor \(\delta ({T_j})\) is determined based on the outdoor temperature and the ratio of heating capacity to electrical power consumption.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the conditions for \(\delta ({T_j})\) to be 0?
output: \(\delta ({T_j})\) is 0 if \({T_j} \le {T_{off}}\) or if the ratio of heating capacity to electrical power consumption is less than 1.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the conditions for \(\delta ({T_j})\) to be 1/2?
output: \(\delta ({T_j})\) is 1/2 if \({T_{off}} < {T_j} \le {T_{on}}\) and the ratio of heating capacity to electrical power consumption is greater than or equal to 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the condition for \(\delta ({T_j})\) to be 1?
output: \(\delta ({T_j})\) is 1 if \({T_j} > {T_{on}}\) and the ratio of heating capacity to electrical power consumption is greater than or equal to 1.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does \({T_{off}}\) represent?
output: \({T_{off}}\) is the outdoor temperature when the compressor is automatically shut off.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does \({T_{on}}\) represent?
output: \({T_{on}}\) is the outdoor temperature when the compressor is automatically turned back on, if applicable.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how can \(\dot{Q}_{h} \cdot ({T_j})\) be calculated?
output: \(\dot{Q}_{h} \cdot ({T_j})\) can be calculated using the specified piecewise equations based on the outdoor temperature.

input: In EnergyPlus, how can \(\dot{E}_{h} \cdot ({T_j})\) be calculated?
output: \(\dot{E}_{h} \cdot ({T_j})\) can be calculated using the specified piecewise equations based on the outdoor temperature.

input: What does the equation \\(\\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}\\) represent in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, \\(\\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}\\) is the ratio of the electrical energy used for resistive space heating during periods when the outdoor temperature fell within the range represented by bin temperature \\({T_j}\\) to the total number of hours (N) in the heating season (W).

input: What is the definition of \\(\\frac{{{n_j}}}{N}\\) in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, \\(\\frac{{{n_j}}}{N}\\) is the fractional bin hours for the heating season; it is the ratio of the number of hours during the heating season when the outdoor temperature fell within the range represented by bin temperature \\({T_j}\\) to the total number of hours in the heating season, dimensionless.

input: What does the equation for building heating load \\(BL({T_j})\\) look like in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the building heating load is evaluated using the equation \\(BL({T_j}) = \\frac{{\\left( {18.33 - {T_j}} \\right)}}{{\\left( {18.33 - {T_{OD}}} \\right)}} \\cdot C \\cdot DHR\\).

input: How is the minimum design heating requirement \\(DHR_{min}\\) calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the minimum design heating requirement is calculated as follows: \\(DHR_{min} = \\left\\{ \\begin{array}{l} {\\dot{Q}_h}(8.33) \\cdot (1.8) \\cdot \\left( {\\frac{{18.33 - {T_{OD}}}}{{60.0}}} \\right), {~for~Regions~I,~II,~III,~IV,~and~VI} \\\\ {\\dot{Q}_h}(8.33),{~for~Region~V} \\end{array} \\right\\}\\).

input: What is the formula for maximum design heating requirement \\(DHR_{max}\\) in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the maximum design heating requirement is given by the equation: \\(DHR_{max} = \\left\\{ \\begin{array}{l} {2 \\cdot \\dot{Q}_h}(8.33) \\cdot (1.8) \\cdot \\left( {\\frac{{18.33 - {T_{OD}}}}{{60.0}}} \\right), {~for~Regions~I,~II,~III,~IV,~and~VI} \\\\ {2.2 \\cdot \\dot{Q}_h}(8.33),{~for~Region~V} \\end{array} \\right\\}\\).

input: What is the equation for the intermediate term used in the calculations of HSPF in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the intermediate term used in the calculations of HSPF is given by \\(\\frac{{{e_h}({T_j})}}{N} = \\frac{{X({T_j}) \\cdot \\mathop {{E_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j}) \\cdot \\delta ({T_j})}}{{PL{F_j}}} \\cdot \\frac{{{n_j}}}{N\\).

input: How is the ratio \\(\\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}\\) expressed in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, \\(\\frac{{RH({T_j})}}{N}\\) is expressed as \\(\\left[ {BL({T_j}) - \\left( {X({T_j}) \\cdot \\mathop {{Q_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j}) \\cdot \\delta ({T_j})} \\right)} \\right] \\cdot \\frac{{{n_j}}}{N}\\).

input: What does the equation for the heating mode load factor \\(X({T_j})\\) look like in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the heating mode load factor is defined as \\(X({T_j}) = \\left\\{ \\begin{array}{l} BL({T_J})/\\mathop {{Q_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j}) \\\\ {\\rm{or}} \\\\ 1 \\end{array} \\right\\}\\), whichever is less.

input: What is the formula for the part load factor \\(PL{F_j}\\) in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the part load factor is determined as follows: \\(PL{F_j} = 1 - {C_{{D^h}}}[1 - X({T_j})]\\).

input: How is the low temperature cut-out factor \\(\\delta ({T_j})\\) determined in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the low temperature cut-out factor is determined as follows: \\(\\delta ({T_j}) = \\left\\{ \\begin{array}{l} {\\rm{0,~if~}}{T_j} \\le {T_{off}}{\\rm{~or~}}\\frac{{\\mathop {{Q_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j})}}{{\\mathop {{E_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j})}} < 1 \\\\ {\\rm{1/2,~if~}}{T_{off}} < {T_j} \\le {T_{on}}{\\rm{~and~}}\\frac{{\\mathop {{Q_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j})}}{{\\mathop {{E_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j})}} \\ge 1 \\\\ {\\rm{1,~if~}}{T_j} > {T_{on}}{\\rm{~and~}}\\frac{{\\mathop {{Q_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j})}}{{\\mathop {{E_h}}\\limits^ \\cdot  ({T_j})}} \\ge 1 \\end{array} \\right.\\).

input: What is the equation used to calculate \\(\\dot{Q}_{h}({T_j})\\) in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, \\(\\dot{Q}_{h}({T_j})\\) is calculated using the equation: \\(\\dot{Q}_{h}({T_j}) = \\left\\{ \\begin{array}{l}\\dot{Q}_{h}(-8.33) + \\frac{{\\left[ {\\dot{{Q}_{h}}(8.33) - \\dot{{Q_h}}(-8.33)} \\right] \\cdot \\left( {{T_j} + 8.33} \\right)}}{{16.67}}{\\rm{,~if~}}{T_j} \\ge 7.22^{\\circ}C {\\rm{~or~}}{T_j} \\le  -8.33^{\\circ}C \\\\ \\dot{Q}_{h}(-8.33) + \\frac{{\\left[ {\\dot{Q}_{h}(1.67) - \\dot{Q}_{h}(-8.33)} \\right] \\cdot \\left( {{T_j} + 8.33} \\right)}}{{10}}{\\rm{,~if~}} -8.33^{\\circ}C < {T_j} < 7.22^{\\circ}C\\end{array} \\right.\\).

input: How is \\(\\dot{E}_{h}({T_j})\\) calculated in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, \\(\\dot{E}_{h}({T_j})\\) is calculated using the equation: \\(\\dot{E}_{h}({T_j}) = \\left\\{ \\begin{array}{l}\\dot{E}_{h}(-8.33) + \\frac{{\\left[ {\\dot{{E}_{h}}(8.33) - \\dot{{E_h}}(-8.33)} \\right] \\cdot \\left( {{T_j} + 8.33} \\right)}}{{16.67}}{\\rm{,~if~}}{T_j} \\ge 7.22^{\\circ}C {\\rm{~or~}}{T_j} \\le  -8.33^{\\circ}C \\\\ \\dot{E}_{h}(-8.33) + \\frac{{\\left[ {\\dot{E}_{h}(1.67) - \\dot{E}_{h}(-8.33)} \\right] \\cdot \\left( {{T_j} + 8.33} \\right)}}{{10}}{\\rm{,~if~}} -8.33^{\\circ}C < {T_j} < 7.22^{\\circ}C\\end{array} \\right.\\).

In EnergyPlus, what is the object name used to simulate the performance of a multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil?
output: The object name is Coil:Heating:DX:MultiSpeed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how many discrete compressor speeds can the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model accommodate?
output: The model can accommodate two to four discrete compressor speeds.

input: From EnergyPlus, what performance information is provided for each speed in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model?
output: Each speed has a set of corresponding performance information at rated conditions along with curve fits for variations in total capacity, energy input ratio, and part-load fraction.

input: In EnergyPlus, what determines the full load supply airflow rate for the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil?
output: The full load supply airflow rate is dependent on the speed number and is set by its parent object AirLoopHVAC:UnitaryHeatPump:AirToAir:MultiSpeed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the part-load impact on coil energy use applied in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model?
output: The part-load impact on coil energy use is automatically applied to the lowest speed.

input: From EnergyPlus, what choice is provided regarding part-load impacts on coil energy use when operating at speeds greater than Speed 1?
output: A choice is provided to determine whether part-load impacts on coil energy use are applied when the coil is operating at speeds greater than Speed 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, how are adjustment factors for frost formation calculated in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model?
output: Adjustment factors applied to total capacity and input power to account for frost formation on the outdoor coil are calculated at each speed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what aspects of the indoor DX heating coil's performance does the multi-speed electric heat pump model simulate?
output: The model simulates the thermal performance of the indoor DX heating coil and the power consumption of the outdoor unit, including multispeed compressor, fans, crankcase heaters, and defrost heaters.

input: From EnergyPlus, what factors influence the performance of the indoor supply air fan in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model?
output: The performance of the indoor supply air fan varies widely depending on control strategy, fan type, fan motor efficiency, and pressure losses through the air distribution system.

input: In EnergyPlus, does the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model account for the thermal effects or electric power consumption of the indoor supply air fan?
output: No, the DX system model does not account for the thermal effects or electric power consumption of the indoor supply air fan.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how can the indoor fan configurations be linked with the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model?
output: EnergyPlus contains separate models for simulating the performance of various indoor fan configurations, which can be easily linked with the DX system model.

input: From EnergyPlus, how does the performance of the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model at Speed 1 compare to that of the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed model?
output: When the model determines performance at Speed 1 or cycling between OFF and Speed 1, its performance is almost the same as the performance for the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed model.

input: In EnergyPlus, how are outlet conditions calculated differently in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model compared to the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed model?
output: The outlet conditions are calculated slightly differently, even though the performance is almost the same.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model determine performance at higher speeds?
output: The model linearly interpolates the performance at two consecutive speeds (n-1 and n) as needed to meet the heating load, with the fraction of time at each speed established by the speed ratio.

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens when single mode operation is specified at higher speeds in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model?
output: Its performance is almost the same as the performance for the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed model at different flow rate and capacity with the given speed number, and no linear interpolation is performed between two adjacent speeds.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the highest speed used for each HVAC timestep when single mode operation is specified at higher speeds?
output: The highest speed which does not exceed the sensible load is used for each HVAC timestep.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the exception in calculation procedures for Speed 1 operation in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model?
output: The exception is the outlet node condition calculation when the supply air fan operation mode is ContinuousFanWithCyclingCompressor.

input: From EnergyPlus, what inputs does the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model require that differ from the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed object?
output: The multispeed model requires a set of fields at each speed, such as rated capacity, rated COP, two capacity modifiers, two energy input ratio modifiers, and part-load correction.

input: In EnergyPlus, what additional inputs are included in the multi-speed electric heat pump DX air heating coil model that are not available in the Coil:Heating:DX:SingleSpeed object?
output: The inputs include waste heat fraction and modifier as a function of temperature to calculate recoverable waste heat for heat recovery.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the formula for calculating total delivered heating capacity for speed 1 operating at the cycling ratio needed to meet the requested heating load?
output: {Q_{coil,cycling}} = {\dot{m}_{Speed~1}}\left( {CycRatio} \right)({h_{inlet}} - {h_{outlet,full}})

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does Q_{coil,cycling} represent?
output: Q_{coil,cycling} is the delivered sensible heating capacity for Speed 1 operating at a specific cycling ratio (W).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the air mass flow rate through the heating coil at Speed 1 denoted?
output: \\dot{m}_{Speed~1} is the air mass flow rate through the heating coil at Speed 1 as set by the parent object (kg/s).

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air during full-load operation at Speed 1 referred to as?
output: h_{outlet,full} is the specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air during full-load operation at Speed 1 (no cycling) (J/kg).

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the specific enthalpy of the coil inlet air represented?
output: h_{inlet} is the specific enthalpy of the coil inlet air (J/kg).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does CycRatio represent?
output: CycRatio is the cycling ratio at Speed 1, the ratio of requested heating load to the full-load capacity of the coil at Speed 1 (dimensionless).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is assumed about the heating capacity of the coil when it is OFF?
output: It is assumed that the coil provides no heating capacity when the coil is OFF, even if the supply air fan continues to operate.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the average specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air calculated?
output: The average specific enthalpy of the coil outlet air is calculated based on the delivered sensible heating capacity and the average air mass flow rate entering the coil.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the average outlet air enthalpy calculated?
output: h_{outlet,average} = h_{inlet} - \\frac{Q_{coil,cycling}}{\\dot{m}_{inlet}}.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does h_{outlet,average} represent?
output: h_{outlet,average} is the average specific enthalpy at the coil outlet (J/kg).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is \\dot{m}_{inlet}?
output: \\dot{m}_{inlet} is the mass flow rate at the inlet to the coil as established by the parent object.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the average outlet air temperature calculated?
output: The average outlet air temperature is calculated based on the inlet air humidity ratio and the average outlet air enthalpy using the psychrometric function PsyTdbFnHW.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the relationship between the heating coil's outlet air humidity ratio and the inlet air humidity ratio?

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the total delivered heating capacity at Speed n-1 calculated?

input: What is the equation for full load outlet air specific enthalpy at Speed n in EnergyPlus?

input: What is the equation for full load outlet air specific enthalpy at Speed n-1 in EnergyPlus?

input: What is the equation for full load energy input at Speed n in EnergyPlus?

input: What is the equation for full load energy input at Speed n-1 in EnergyPlus?

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the HeatingPower calculated when the input for 'Apply Part Load Fraction to Speeds Greater than 1' is Yes?

input: In EnergyPlus, how are the industry standard ratings for multi-speed direct expansion heating coils calculated?

According to EnergyPlus, is the rated Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER) calculated for any DX Heating Coils?

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value for Rated Supply Fan Power Per Volume Flow Rate if the user leaves the input field blank?

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the HSPF for multi-speed compressor heat pumps calculated?
output: The HSPF for multi-speed compressor heat pumps in Btu/W-h is calculated using the provided equation involving building space conditioning load and heating requirements.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does BL(T\(_{j}\)) represent in the HSPF equation?
output: BL(T\(_{j}\)) is the building space conditioning load corresponding to an outdoor temperature of T\(_{j}\).

input: What is the equation for the Heating Seasonal Performance Factor (HSPF) for multi-speed compressor heat pumps in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the HSPF is given by HSPF = \\frac{{\\sum\\limits_{j}^{M} {\\frac{{n_j}}{N} \\cdot BL\\left( {T_j} \\right)} }}{{\\sum\\limits_{j}^{M} {\\frac{{e_h\\left( {T_j} \\right)}}{N}{\\rm{ + }}} \\sum\\limits_{j}^{M} {\\frac{{RH\\left( {T_j} \\right)}}{N}} }} \\cdot {F_{def}}

input: In EnergyPlus, what does e_h(T_j)/N represent?
output: It is the ratio of the electrical energy consumed by the heat pump during periods of the space heating season when the outdoor temperature fell within the range represented by bin temperature T_j to the total number of hours (N) in the heating season.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what additional electrical energy may be included in the e_h(T_j)/N ratio for heat pumps with a heat comfort controller?
output: This ratio may also include electrical energy used by resistive elements to maintain a minimum air delivery temperature.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is RH(T_j)/N defined?
output: It is the ratio of the electrical energy used for resistive space heating during periods when the outdoor temperature fell within the range represented by bin temperature T_j to the total number of hours (N) in the heating season.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is resistive space heating modeled?
output: Resistive space heating is modeled as being used to meet that portion of the building load that the heat pump does not meet because of insufficient capacity or because the heat pump automatically turns off at the lowest outdoor temperatures.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is T_j?

input: From EnergyPlus, what does n_j/N represent?

input: In EnergyPlus, what does j represent?
output: j is the bin number.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does M stand for?
output: M is the total number of temperature bins for each generalized climatic region.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the demand defrost credit represented?

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the building heating load calculated?
